data.body:
Triage before close (2026-08-06 23:15 UTC).

The canary fired because the Reconcile Bridge workflow is **intentionally disabled**, not because of an infrastructure outage. GitHub reports workflow 302389202 (.github/workflows/reconcile-bridge.yml) state=disabled_manually. Ticket ed5e records that operators disabled it deliberately on 2026-08-04 to stop the reconciler parent-clear defect from destroying more parent edges.

Heartbeat gap itself is closed: four reconcile passes succeeded within the last hour (22:15, 22:32, 22:44, 22:51 UTC).

The two most recent runs (22:58 dispatch, 23:01 schedule) fail, but NOT in reconcile — the reconcile work completes and the run then dies in the RECONCILE_CONTINUOUS self-redispatch step: 'could not create workflow dispatch event: HTTP 422: Cannot trigger a workflow_dispatch on a disabled workflow'. That is a direct consequence of the deliberate disable, not a new fault.

Closing as env_integration: the reported condition was an intentional maintenance state. AC #1 ('reconcile-bridge.yml is running and its most recent run succeeded') cannot be literally satisfied while the bridge is intentionally off, so this closes via force-close with that reason recorded.
